newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies German residents threatened by row.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies German residents threatened by row.

text.p: Iran on Wednesday denied Germans in the country were under threat because of a row between Tehran and Bonn over a German prosecutor accusing Iranian leaders of ordering the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
An Iranian foreign ministry spokesman, quoted by Iranian television, denied "rumours spread by certain media that German citizens were under threat in Iran".
"To misrepresent Iran as unsafe for German citizens' lives is a vain attempt to distort the just popular protests against the defamation by the (German) court," the spokesman said.

In one of several anti-German demonstrations on Wednesday, Islamic seminary students and teachers marched in the holy city of Qom to protest against the charges which they denounced as "a plot against the sanctities of all Moslems of the world", the Iranian news agency IRNA said.
About 1,000 hardline Islamic protesters rallied outside the German embassy in Tehran on Tuesday, chanting "The German prosecutor should be executed".
Iran, which has denied any involvement in the shootings, appeared to be trying to defuse the row on Wednesday.
Supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei said in a speech the United States and Israel were Iran's main enemies and disputes with other countries were secondary.

Khamenei did not mention Germany by name but regional analysts said the speech looked like an attempt to defuse the row with Bonn over the prosecutor's charge that Khamenei and other Tehran officials ordered the killing of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator at a Berlin restaurant in 1992.
Newspapers carried statements by various groups, with some radical groups urging the government to sever ties with Germany if it did not apologise for the accusations.

The row threatens trade ties worth $1.4 billion last year between Iran and Germany. Also at risk is the European Union's "critical dialogue" with Iran which Bonn has promoted as an alternative to U.S. sanctions aimed at isolating Tehran.
Tehran officially protested last week to Bonn over the charges. German prosecutors have demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese who were tried for the killings.
